source.title: Open problems for the superKdV equations

accepted.question_text: Construct an integrable supersymmetric extension of the Korteweg-de Vries equation with an odd Poisson structure in which the bosonic evolution equations still couple nontrivially to the fermionic fields, unlike the then-known odd N = 2 example where the bosonic fields do not interact with the fermions in their time evolution.

evidence.quote: A new N = 2 super KdV equation with an odd Poisson structure has been found recently in [7] but the resulting equations are somewhat less interesting in that the bosonic fields do not couple to the fermions in their time evolution. It would be of interest to see whether there are other ‘odd’ integrable extensions displaying fermionic interactions in the bosonic evolution equations.

accepted.question_text: Find an integrable deformation of the N = 1 supersymmetric KdV equation whose deformation mechanism reproduces the fermionic nonlocal conservation laws that arise for the super KdV system.

evidence.quote: OP-1: Find an integrable deformation that reproduces the fermionic nonlocal conservation laws.

accepted.question_text: For each of the three integrable N = 2 supersymmetric KdV equations SKdV_a with a in {-2, 1, 4}, find an integrable deformation of the Miura-type structure that reproduces the conservation laws of these hierarchies.

evidence.quote: Although there exists a Miura transformation, there are no known integrable (i.e., Gardner-type) deformations of it. This leads us to: OP-2: Find an integrable deformation for SKdV−2,1,4 that reproduces their conservations laws.

accepted.question_text: For the N = 2 supersymmetric KdV equations SKdV_{-2} and SKdV_4, determine how the fermionic nonlocal conservation laws are encoded by, or derived from, the corresponding Lax operator, given that the known Lax operators have two distinct fourth roots but the connection to those fermionic conservation laws is not understood.

evidence.quote: For a = −2, 4, there are two independent towers of fermionic nonlocal conservations laws [18]... However, although the Lax operator has two distinct fourth roots, these have not yet been related to these fermionic conservation laws: OP-3: For SKdV−2,4, find the relation between the fermionic nonlocal conservation laws and the Lax operator.

accepted.question_text: Explain why the N = 2 supersymmetric KdV equation SKdV_1 has the first fermionic conservation laws but does not generate infinite towers of fermionic conservation laws, in contrast with the a = -2 and a = 4 cases.

evidence.quote: On the other hand, for the a = 1 case, the first fermionic laws (3.9) do not generate infinite towers: they are isolated. OP-4: Why there are no infinite towers of fermionic conservation laws for SKdV1?

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the N = 2 supersymmetric KdV equation SKdV_1 is bihamiltonian, namely whether it admits a first Hamiltonian structure making it part of a bihamiltonian integrable hierarchy like the a = -2 and a = 4 cases.

evidence.quote: In that respect, the SKdV1 stands as one of the rare example of classical integrable system which is not (known to be) bihamiltonian. OP-5: Is SKdV1 bihamiltonian?

accepted.question_text: Explain why there are exactly three integrable N = 2 supersymmetric KdV extensions, and determine whether this threefold classification has an underlying Lie-algebraic explanation, for example one related to the existence of the three classical algebras.

evidence.quote: OP-6: Why is there exactly three integrable N = 2 super KdV extensions? Is there an underlying Lie algebraic interpretation for this threefold way (i.e, is this related to the existence of the three classical algebras)?

accepted.question_text: Develop a formulation of the Painlevé analysis directly in superspace for supersymmetric integrable systems, rather than only in ordinary component variables.

evidence.quote: As stressed here, these equations are naturally formulated in superspace. Over the years, it became clear that a lot of structure is contained in the Painlevé test: for instance its truncation leads to Backl̈und transformations and the Lax operator [20]. Yet, no Painlevé analysis has been done directly in superspace. OP-7: Is it possible to formulate the Painlevé analysis in superspace?

accepted.question_text: Develop solution theory for N = 2 supersymmetric integrable systems, in particular Darboux transformations and related explicit solution-generating methods analogous to those already known in the N = 1 case.
accepted.context_brief: solutions for N=2 super integrable systems

evidence.quote: Moreover, little is known concerning the solutions of super integrable systems. The Darboux transformation in the N = 1 case has been worked out in [21] but nothing has been done at this point concerning the N = 2 cases.

accepted.question_text: Clarify the geometric relation between supersymmetric integrable systems and soliton theory, especially by determining the super-geometric structures associated with the super KdV equations and their super Sine-Gordon relatives.

evidence.quote: Finally, unravelling the deep relations between geometry and soliton theory has been an important theme of this workshop; little is known on the super version of this connection. In particular, the super KdV equations have super Sine-Gordon relatives and these should lead to very interesting geometrical structures.
